newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil rally not finished yet - chartists.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil rally not finished yet - chartists.

text.p: IPE gas oil may not have reached the high yet for this year's rally, even though the market has gained more than 40 percent since May and the spot contract touched a five-year peak on Friday, technical analysts said.
Daily and weekly indicators will continue to flash bullish signs for the Oct contract once Sept expires on Thursday.
That means any wicked downside correction, which chartists are bracing for because the market is overbought and extremely volatile, would not be bearish for Oct, they said.
Oct is trading at an $11 discount to Sept, so when Sept expires, Oct will have breathing room to go higher on the continuation chart, they added.
"It is bullish until it breaks trend and there is no sign of it breaking trend," said Nick Wilson, technical analyst at MeesPierson.

His target for Oct gas oil is $221.50 a tonne, a swing objective. He subtracted $159, a support level from earlier this summer, from resistance at $190.25, a high from August 23. He took that difference and added to $190.25 to get $221.50.
"Technically there are supportive gaps underneath that are bullish and the long-term (signs) are bullish," said Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden in London.
"But in the short term the market is getting a bit carried away with itself."
"We're talking about a very strong bull market but an overbought market," he said.
At 1046 GMT, Sept was up $5.25 at $218 and Oct traded $3.25 higher at $207.

Oct gas oil gapped higher on Monday from $196.25 to $198.50. It was briefly broken on Wednesday before rallying on Thursday and gapping higher today. But it has not yet been able to test its contract high of $210.50 touched on Tuesday.
Sept gas oil also gapped higher twice this week and today reached $219.50, a contract high and the strongest for the spot futures since $223 in November 1991.
The spot contract's lifetime peak is $363 in October 1990 after Iraq invaded Kuwait.
The spot contract's rally from $155.25 on May 24 to today's high marks more than a 40 percent advance.
Wilson expected his objective to be reached over the next two weeks or so but added, "I don't rule out a current consolidation correcting to $196.25 to close that gap before it moves ahead."
Some analysts described Monday's gap as a breakaway gap, making today's gap a measurement or runaway gap. A third gap, if it occurs, would be an exhaustion gap that would signal a top was at hand.

The nine- and 14-day relative strength index levels are currently about 87 and 84 percent. Chartists said these were extremely overbought levels but also cautioned that in strong bull markets or rallies that appear to be overextended, these indicators are not reliable for picking a top.
"As previously stated, we're near a major top, but there is still no evidence that a top is in place," Al Graham of Elliott Wave International said in his daily report, out before the open.

"Even though we covered a lot of ground down from $210.50 (basis Oct) into Tuesday's close, wave internals within that fall are not yet unmistakably impulsive, and that leaves the door open for another high," said Graham in Gainesville, Georgia.
He put Oct's resistance above $210.50 at $216.50-$217.75 and $221.75 and support at $199, $197.75 and $196.25-$195.25.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8185
